about: Question bank for the AI Intake Interview. Every field the matching engine and outreach need, with a required level and how to ask. Diff this against the app's existing intake questions (see docs/INTAKE.md), don't replace them blindly.

priority_levels.required: The match can't run correctly without it. The interview can't finish without an answer.
priority_levels.required_ask: Must be asked. 'None' or 'not yet' is a valid answer, but silence isn't: a missing answer can put a conflicted or already-pitched fund on the list.
priority_levels.recommended: Changes who is on the list or how strong the outreach is. Ask; accept 'skip'.
priority_levels.optional: Nice to have. Ask only if the conversation allows, or collect from the deck.

questions.ask: What's the company called?
questions.why: Outreach and reporting.

questions.ask: What's your website?
questions.why: Lets the interviewer pre-fill answers from the site, and goes into outreach.
questions.validate: Must look like a domain. If they have no site yet, accept 'none' and take the deck link instead.

questions.ask: In one sentence: what do you do, and for whom?
questions.why: Basis for the sector mapping and every outreach opener.
questions.validate: Max ~25 words. If it's longer, propose a tightened version back and ask them to confirm.

questions.ask: Who pays you: businesses, consumers, both, or are you a marketplace?
questions.why: Sanity-checks the sector choice; some funds are B2B-only or consumer-only.

questions.ask: What round are you raising now? Pre-seed, seed, Series A…?
questions.why: The first filter. A wrong stage means the wrong list.
questions.normalize: angel / friends & family / pre-seed → Pre-Seed; seed / seed+ / seed extension / bridge to A → Seed (flag 'extension'); A → Series A; B → Series B; C, D, later → Series C and Beyond; 'growth' → Growth Equity; buyout / sale / recap → PE stages.
questions.validate: Cross-check with revenue and raise amount (see consistency rules in docs/INTAKE.md). If they don't match, read back what you heard and ask which is right.

questions.ask: How much are you raising in this round?
questions.why: Check-size fit: flags funds whose stated checks are too big or too small.
questions.validate: A number with a currency. If it's a range, store the target and note the range.

questions.ask: What instrument: SAFE, convertible note, priced equity, or debt?
questions.why: Filters out lenders vs equity investors.
questions.normalize: SAFE / convertible note / priced round / equity → Equity; venture debt / loan / credit line → Debt; revenue-based financing → Royalties.

questions.ask: Do you have a lead investor for this round, or do you still need one?
questions.why: Without a lead, wave 1 should be firms that lead at this stage.

questions.ask: Is anything committed or soft-circled yet? How much, and from whom?
questions.why: Social proof for outreach; the named investors go on the exclusion list.

questions.ask: Do you have a target valuation or SAFE cap?
questions.why: Lets us drop funds whose valuation bands don't fit (once the DB has them).

questions.ask: When do you want to close? Any hard deadline, like runway?
questions.why: Sets wave timing and follow-up cadence.

questions.ask: What will this round pay for, and what milestone does it get you to?
questions.why: Outreach narrative.

questions.ask: Based on what you told me, investors would file you under {suggestions}. Which is the best fit, and is there a second one?
questions.why: The #1 vertical decides Bullseye. Ranking matters: the first one is the core.
questions.how: Never show the full taxonomy list. Propose 2–3 labels from the one-liner and website, and let the founder confirm or reorder. Map their words to the exact taxonomy labels.

questions.ask: (Usually inferred, not asked.) Confirm: 'So the industry is {derived}. Right?'
questions.why: 44% of funds have no vertical tags; for those, industry is the only sector signal.
questions.how: Derive from the verticals (V2I map in the engine) plus the one-liner. Confirm in the final read-back.

questions.ask: Who's the typical customer: company size, industry, or type of consumer?
questions.why: Sharpens the sector choice and the outreach.

questions.ask: Where is the company headquartered?
questions.why: Most funds invest only in certain geographies.

questions.ask: Which state?
questions.why: US funds are often regional (California, Mid-Atlantic, …).

questions.ask: Which city?
questions.why: Ranks partners based near the founder higher; an in-person meeting matters early.

questions.ask: Where is the company incorporated, e.g. a Delaware C-corp?
questions.why: Many US funds only invest in US (Delaware) entities. Decides whether cross-border US investors are realistic.

questions.ask: Which markets do you sell into today, or plan to enter in the next 12 months?
questions.why: Unlocks cross-border investors, e.g. US funds for an Israeli company entering the US.

questions.ask: Is the team in one place or distributed?
questions.why: Context for investors with local-presence requirements.

questions.ask: Where are you on revenue: pre-revenue, or what's your current MRR or ARR?
questions.why: Checks that the stage is right, and it's the strongest outreach proof.
questions.validate: 'Pre-revenue' is a valid answer. Store currency and period.

questions.ask: How fast is it growing, month over month or year over year?
questions.why: Outreach proof and stage check.

questions.ask: What are the 2–3 proof points you'd lead with? Customers, pilots, users, retention…
questions.why: Goes straight into openers and the angle drafts.

questions.ask: Who are the founders? Roles, relevant background, prior exits or notable companies.
questions.why: At pre-seed and seed, the team is usually the strongest cold-email hook.

questions.ask: How many people are on the team today?
questions.why: Context.

questions.ask: Who has already invested? Funds and notable angels.
questions.why: They go on the exclusion list. Pitching your own investor cold looks careless. They're also social proof.

questions.ask: Which investors have you already talked to in the last 12 months, and how did it go?
questions.why: Re-pitching a fund that passed burns credibility. Fund names go on the exclusion list; outcomes go in notes.

questions.ask: Who are your 2–3 closest competitors?
questions.why: Funds backing a direct competitor usually won't invest; used in the portfolio-conflict check.

questions.ask: Any previous rounds? When, how much, at what valuation?
questions.why: Stage sanity and outreach context.

questions.ask: Are you open to family offices and angel groups, or VC funds only?
questions.why: Sets the investor-type filter; the default comes from stage.

questions.ask: Any investors you don't want approached, or types to avoid (e.g. corporate VCs)?
questions.why: Exclusions and client trust.

questions.ask: Do you already know any investors personally, even loosely?
questions.why: Cross-checked against the match list. Warm paths go first.

questions.ask: Can you share your deck, or a one-pager?
questions.why: Fills gaps automatically and feeds the outreach.
